title: Coast Guard Air Station Cape Cod pilot recounts Hurricane Harvey response one year later
description: Lt. Michelle Cosenza, an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter pilot at Coast Guard Air Station Cape Cod, talks about her experience responding to Hurricane Harvey. Coast Guard crews from around the country, including the Northeast, responded to the disaster and rescued more than 11,000 people. (U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Andrew Barresi)
keywords: MH-60 Jayhawk, Air Station Cape Cod, Hurricane Harvey, helicopter, USCG

transcript.text: (light music)
- [Lt. Michelle Cosenza] I was actually up in Boston
with my friends at a Red Sox game,
and got the call, hey tomorrow morning at 7 am
you're flying out to go down to Houston.
(light music)
I had done a lot of hoisting for practice
up here in the Cape, but I had never done
what we call an operational hoist.
And that means you're going out on SAR case
and hoisting someone, basically not in the Coast Guard.
Knowing that you're saving a life was really exciting.
It was a family of four, a grandmother,
grandfather, a mother, and her baby.
We did three hoists, the mother and the baby
came up first, and this baby was adorable,
and all our flight medic kept saying was
how adorable this baby was.
And she wasn't screaming,
she was just sitting there calm the entire time.
(helicopter whirring)
As a junior pilot, to see this,
and know overall what the Coast Guard
is capable of because we have crews
coming from all over the United States,
we all do the same thing, and it's just great to know
that the practice that we preach
is actually being utilized.
(light music)
